name: the Kindling
why: Supersedes the earlier keep. Fails the prior-work check in context: in an ash world with a warm stone you return to after death, 'kindling' is Dark Souls' word for feeding a bonfire (team/ending-check.jsonl). The first replacement, 'the Assart', was itself replaced by 'the Essart': most players read 'Assart' by its parts, 'ass' and 'art', and a joke on the founding catastrophe's name leaks into every line that uses it (team/ending-check-2.jsonl).
source: Real archaic word (Wolfe rule): essart, the Anglo-French form of English assart, forest land grubbed up and cleared, often by burning, for tillage; assarts and their rents were reckoned at the Exchequer, which fits the Chequer burning the Deep Account to farm warm ground. https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/assart, https://www.etymonline.com/word/assart. Entries cited from the dictionaries' known coverage, not fetched in this pass; no exact-phrase search for a prior work of that name was run (no web access).

name: N4's role word (faith-keeper)
why: 'Faith Keepers' is Frostpunk's own term (team/borrowed-beats.jsonl, B21). The word should carry the job: N4 prays the names of the dead at every burning and keeps the accounts, which is what a bede-roll is.
source: Real archaic word: bedesman (beadsman), a pensioner whose task was to pray for the souls listed on a bede-roll, the register of names to be prayed for. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beadsman (web search, snippet; not an exact-phrase prior-work search).

name: kindle-iron
why: 'kindle-' echoes the retired Kindling and its Dark Souls bonfire reading (names.jsonl, 'the Kindling'); the Essart rename removed its tie.
source: Real dialect/trade word: ruddle (raddle, reddle), a red ochreous iron ore. https://www.wordnik.com/words/ruddle, https://millsarchive.org/glossary/a-z-glossary/4221 (web search, snippets).

name: rib-goat
why: 'rib-' belongs to the dead-god-as-landscape motif the rework removed (team/rework-plan.md, creatures.md).
source: Real outside word: tahr, a Himalayan wild goat, English since 1832 from Nepali thar. https://www.dictionary.com/browse/tahr, https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/tahr (web search, snippets). Fits a shaggy cold-slope goat.

name: ridge-hunter
why: 'ridge-' belongs to the removed dead-god-as-landscape motif.
source: Real archaic word: ounce, from Old French lonce (lynx) with l- misread as the article; used for the snow leopard since the 1770s. A long low pale ambush cat. https://www.etymonline.com/word/ounce, https://www.dictionary.com/browse/ounce (web search, snippets). Unrelated to the unit of weight.

name: ridge-bone
why: 'ridge-' and '-bone' belong to the removed dead-god-as-landscape motif (rework-plan.md: drop the bone-white ridges).
source: Real dialect word: cauk (cawk, calk), Derbyshire miners' name for compact barytes, a pale heavy spar. https://www.derbyshire.gov.uk/site-elements/documents/pdf/environment/planning/planning-policy/minerals-local-plan/vein-minerals-background-paper.pdf, https://www.wiktionary.com/wiki/cauk (web search, snippets).
